findings.reason: the plan must either give the RRF-top-60 labelling its own node, as §3 gave its top-10 labelling one, or state the labelling as an explicit precondition in §7's done-when, so the node's single verdict covers one deliverable.
findings.text: §7 now carries a second deliverable beside the rerank: "this section first labels RRF's top 60 on every question, under §3's rule and into §3's fixture", yet §3 sized exactly that work as its own node ("The harness then takes two nodes, because labelling and code do not fit one hour together") and §7's done-when closes only the rerank's ship decision, so a node could ship with the labelling half-done and neither verdict would catch it

findings.reason: a node reading §7's first paragraph would look for the question text in the prototype instead of writing it from the five levels into the harness, and would find nothing.
findings.text: §7 says the product rerank "gets the role-aware question from the prototype", but §3 states "The prototype did not keep its role-aware question text, so write it from §7's five levels and keep it in the harness", and the prototype directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/imas-codex/signal-search-prototype/`) holds only `arms.json`, `embedding_drift.json`, `fig_signal_search_arms.py` and `goldens_draft.json` — no question text — so the mechanism §7 names reaches an artifact that does not exist, and §7's own third paragraph now says the harness keeps it

findings.reason: the plan's operational instruction (call the harness arm functions from a run outside pytest) is unaffected and reaches the same place through the env-var gate, so the false premise misleads a reader but does not send the node down a different path.
findings.text: §7 states "the suite's guard refuses paid requests inside a test process" as its reason for scoring the rerank arms from a measurement run outside pytest, but the harness implements no such guard: it gates the two Jev arms behind the opt-in environment variable `SSFMS_JEV_ARMS` (tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py) and otherwise returns the fused pool order without spending

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the code anchors §7 names (`rerank_candidates`, `_RERANK_QUESTION`) exist, and the plan's hrefs resolve as `<path>.html`; the one unresolvable citation is reported against the reasoning item.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §7's done-when is unchanged by this review's unit (only its third paragraph changed) and measures the rerank against fusion alone with a ship decision that can go either way; the labelling it now carries is enforced by §3's refusal guard.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7 names no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path; its evidence fragment convention matches the sibling sections.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §7's changed text introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's stated source of the role-aware question and its stated reason for scoring outside pytest do not match what the repository and the prototype hold.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §7 now owns labelling RRF's top 60 into §3's fixture as well as implementing and scoring the rerank, while its gate closes only the ship decision.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §7's dependency on §4 is declared in the followup ("§7 follows §4"), and its use of §3's fixture and rule is stated in §7's own text, so the relationships it needs resolve.
